A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TimeSAE research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison across the substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and real-world experiments, explanation-method comparisons, distribution-shift evaluations, and architectural and loss ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds distribution-shift, tabular-transfer, foundation-model, and causal-effect alignment results.

M1.justification: The sparse autoencoder architecture, JumpReLU/TopK mechanisms, decompositional decoder, four-term training objective, and intervention and alignment algorithms are retained. The new applications do not document a modified method.

E1.justification: v2 adds four tabular classification datasets: Adult, Heart Disease, Breast Cancer, and Wine Quality. Table 1 also adds ETTh1→ETTm1, Weather→ETTh1, PAMAP2→OPPORTUNITY, and elite→intermediate EliteLJ evaluations, substantially expanding temporal-resolution, domain, and population coverage.

E2.justification: The established quantitative explainer comparator sets are retained. v2 Figure 4 adds IG to the TimeFM/ETTh1 qualitative comparison, whereas v1 Figures 8–9 showed TimeSAE variants alone for that forecasting example. Chronos 2 and Toto are additional explained predictors, not explanation baselines.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include Chronos 2 and Toto as explained predictors, single-loss and additional loss-removal controls in Table 3, and magnitude-alignment assessment using Pearson correlation, R2, NMAE, and MSE in Tables 6–7. The previously documented dataset splits and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds broader shift-robustness tests and magnitude-faithfulness analyses, and replaces the five-dataset loss-ablation plot with a more extensive component study on FreqShapes. The original counterfactual-error versus faithfulness correlation plot is removed. Existing backbone, hyperparameter, and JumpReLU/TopK analyses remain, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v2 Table 6 explicitly reports FreqShapes Spearman correlation as 0.94±0.02, where v1 Appendix A.3 reported only 0.94. Both retain the ten-seed mean/standard-deviation convention and paired t-tests at the 5% level; an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: Substantial results are added for the new shifts, ablations, magnitude analyses, predictors, and tabular datasets. For the retained ETTh1→ETTh2 setting, TimeX AUPRC changes from 0.401±0.035 in v1 Table 2 to 0.611±0.041 in v2 Table 1; TimeSAE remains 0.641±0.03. However, v2 Table 18 also retains the original values, leaving conflicting reports within v2.

T1.justification: The definitions, Theorem 1, assumptions, and Appendix A.2 proof—including the approximation-error bound—are mathematically unchanged. New Appendix A.4 discusses and empirically applies the existing bound rather than introducing a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introductory contribution claims remain substantively unchanged. The conclusion adds a broader Causal Mechanistic Interpretability framing, claiming actionable counterfactual interpretation and connections to probing, circuit analysis, and equation discovery.

C2.justification: v2 broadens interpretation to magnitude faithfulness and applicability beyond time series. It newly argues that all four losses are necessary and complementary and that consistency drives OOD robustness. Appendix A.4 qualifies OOD magnitude alignment as observational rather than guaranteed. The existing dataset-size and hyperparameter limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The reported code/data access point changes from an anonymous repository to the named project website. Appendix D revises the computing description from three A100 GPUs to primary JAX/TPU training with PyTorch/A100 validation. Existing architecture tables, hyperparameters, and pseudocode are retained.

R1.justification: Focused additions connect the work to mechanistic interpretability and equation discovery, including Templeton, Olah, Brunton, and Pervez citations. Additional Oublal and Bertholom references expand concept-learning and foundation-model context. The original related-work organization and principal positioning remain.

P1.justification: Most prose and section progression are retained. Edits include the title, author information, encoder/explainer terminology, shortened sparsity discussion, an added concluding discussion, impact statement and acknowledgments, and removal of the appendix contents list.

P2.justification: The main text adopts a two-column conference layout, with substantially reorganized displays and new evaluation tables. v1 Figure 11 is split into v2 Figures 9–10, the sparsity-efficiency figure moves to the appendix, and the main composite figure replaces its loss-ablation panel with the TimeFM/IG example.

improvement.justification: The broader evaluations and expanded component study could strengthen the paper, but their evidential gain is unclear. v2 introduces conflicting results for the same stated settings in Tables 1 and 18, while new transfer experiments lack important protocol details. Table 7 reports effect-alignment statistics despite acknowledging unavailable causal ground truth, without explaining the reference effects. These issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
